text:
I need an email to win back customers who cancelled. I own a home cleaning company with 18 cleaners.

What's true:
- We have 212 regular customers. 64 cancelled in the last year. In exit surveys, the most common reason was price, then a different cleaner showing up each time.
- An every-other-week cleaning for a 3-bedroom house costs $165 with us. The app services in our area charge about $140.
- Our cleaners are employees, not contractors. We pay $21 an hour and carry insurance on every visit.
- Last year 7 of our 18 cleaners left, so about 4 in 10 customers had their regular cleaner change at least once.
- We now give each customer a regular cleaner and a named backup.
- Returning customers get their first cleaning for $99.

I want the email to promise that you'll get the same cleaner every single time. Keep it to about 150 words.

I can write this, but I'd advise against the "same cleaner every single time" promise. Your own facts don't back it up.

**The problem with that promise:** Your new system is a regular cleaner *plus a named backup*. The backup exists because the regular won't always be able to come. Last year 7 of your 18 cleaners left. The first time a backup shows up, a customer who left over cleaner changes will see a broken promise, and they won't come back a second time.

**What your facts do support:** "You'll have your own regular cleaner. When they can't make it, it's your named backup, someone you know by name, never a stranger." That deals directly with the reason these people left, and it's a promise you can keep. A skeptical reader will still think "you had turnover before," so I'd like to answer that in the email rather than skip it.

Which version do you want? And a few questions so I don't have to guess:

1. **Has turnover improved since you added the regular-plus-backup setup?** For example, cleaners who've stayed six months or more, or anything you changed to keep them, like a raise. This is the best answer to "why would it be different now?"
2. **What does the customer pay after the $99 first visit?** Back to $165, or is there a returning-customer rate? People who left over price will want to know before they book.
3. **How does the backup work in practice?** Can customers meet the backup or see their name ahead of time? Do you tell them in advance when the backup is coming?
4. **What does "insured on every visit" mean for the customer?** For example, if something gets broken, is it covered? That's what makes the $25 gap with the app services worth paying.
5. **Does the $99 offer have a deadline, how do people book, and who signs the email?**
6. **Is there anything these customers already know or will find out?** For example, the cleaner some of them liked may be one of the 7 who left.

Answer whichever ones you can. I'll write it without any you skip, and I won't fill in made-up details.

Go with the regular cleaner plus named backup version. I know I can't promise the same cleaner every time because of sick days and holidays, but make it as strong as you can without saying anything false.

1. Yes. We started giving each customer a regular cleaner in July, and since then only 1 of our 18 cleaners has left. I don't have anything else on retention, like a raise.
2. I don't know yet.
3. I don't know the details on that.
4. I don't know exactly what's covered. What I do know is the app services around here mostly use contractors who carry no insurance on the visit.
5. The $99 offer ends December 31. They book by replying to the email or calling 555-0164. It's from me, Lisa Grant, owner of Brightway Home Cleaning.
6. I don't know.

I've written it with the regular cleaner and named backup. Each claim in it comes from what you told me.

<final_document>
Subject: Your own cleaner, and a named backup

Hello,

When customers left Brightway this past year, the two reasons we heard most were price and a different cleaner showing up each time. The second one was on us. Last year 7 of our 18 cleaners left, and about 4 in 10 customers saw their cleaner change.

So in July we changed how we work. Every customer now has their own regular cleaner, plus a named backup for sick days and holidays. Since then, only 1 of our 18 cleaners has left.

On price: an every-other-week clean of a 3-bedroom home is $165 with us, about $25 more than the app services. That's because our cleaners are employees, paid $21 an hour and insured on every visit. Most app services here use contractors with no insurance on the visit.

If you come back, your first cleaning is $99. The offer ends December 31. Reply to this email or call 555-0164.

Lisa Grant
Owner, Brightway Home Cleaning
</final_document>

- **Length:** It's about 165 words, a bit over your 150. The extra words go to admitting last year's turnover. These customers lived through it, so I think owning up to it earns trust for the July change. If you need to cut, the 7-of-18 sentence can go.
- **Price after the $99 visit:** The email doesn't say, because you don't know yet. It's the first thing people who left over price will ask. If you can settle it before sending, one sentence would make the email stronger.
- **How strong I could make it:** "Only 1 of 18 has left since July" is your best evidence, so I stated it plainly. But it covers only about four months, so the email doesn't say the change caused it.
- **Unused details:** I left out "you'll always know who's coming" and anything about what the insurance covers, since you weren't sure about either. If you confirm customers are told their backup's name ahead of time, that line is worth adding.
- **Greeting:** It's "Hello" because I didn't have a merge field. If your email tool supports one, swap in first names.
